He promoted the dignity of labor.

questions.text: What were the philosophies propounded by Shankaracharya?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the philosophies propounded by Shankaracharya? (A)

answer.value:
Shankaracharya deeply studied the Upanishads and Brahmasutras and propagated Advaita philosophy.
He gave less importance to worldly life and emphasized the spiritual realm.
He called the world an illusion (maya); Brahman is the ultimate truth.
People, unaware of their inner self (Atman), search for God in the external world.
According to Shankaracharya, Atman and Paramatman (God) are one, hence “Aham Brahmasmi” (I am Brahman or God).
Thus, one must follow the path of knowledge to realize the nature of the world.
Ultimately, one’s Atman must merge with the ultimate truth, Brahman, to attain moksha (liberation).
Shankaracharya taught that God has no attributes, form, or change (Nirguna, Nirakara, Nirvikara).

questions.text: Explain the teachings of Madhvacharya.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the teachings of Madhvacharya. (A)

answer.value:
Madhvacharya propagated Dvaita philosophy.
According to this philosophy, the human soul and divine soul are separate.
To spread his philosophy, he traveled to various places and participated in debates.
He retrieved a statue of Lord Krishna hidden in a mound of sandalwood paste and installed it in Udupi.
He appointed ascetics to perform regular worship of Krishna and established eight monasteries, known as Ashta Mathas.
According to Madhvacharya, the world is not an illusion but as real as the divine soul.
The divine soul is independent, while the rest of the world is illusory.
The divine soul and human soul have a master-servant relationship.
Lord Vishnu or Narayana is the supreme deity.
Worshipping Vishnu elevates the human soul and leads to moksha.

questions.text: What were the reforms introduced by Basavanna in Kalyana?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the reforms introduced by Basavanna in Kalyana? (A)

answer.value:
Basavanna condemned prevailing rituals, superstitions, and blind beliefs.
He played a key role in bringing economic, social, and religious reforms.
Along with societal reform, he worked for spiritual upliftment.
Basavanna introduced the concept of the body as a temple and knowledge as the guru, advocating the idea of one God in the form of Ishtalinga.
He introduced concepts like kayaka (work), dasoha (charity), and Ishtalinga.
He declared, “The eternal perishes, the transient endures,” and “The body is the abode of Shiva” (Kayaka is Kailasa).
He emphasized work and upheld the culture of labor, stating that no work is superior or inferior.
Through the principle of dasoha, he eliminated the culture of hoarding.
He promoted women’s freedom and equality.
Vachanas were written for the spiritual development and welfare of the nation.
Vachana poets highlighted societal flaws and raised awareness among people.

questions.text: What were the philosophies propounded by Ramanujacharya?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the philosophies propounded by Ramanujacharya? (A)

answer.value:
Ramanujacharya advocated the path of devotion (Bhakti Marga) for liberation.
His main teaching was devotion.
He condemned the caste system and allowed devotees of all castes to enter temples, calling untouchables “Sri Hari’s descendants.”
His philosophy is called “Vishishtadvaita,” and the religion he propagated is “Sri Vaishnavism,” so his followers are called Sri Vaishnavas.
He taught that Brahman controls life and nature, and Atman and Paramatman cannot coexist simultaneously.
Devotion and surrender (Prapatti) are essential for attaining moksha.
Ramanujacharya condemned casteism and taught the path of devotion to people of all castes.
He advised renouncing desires and surrendering to God.

Ramanujacharya condemned casteism and taught the path of devotion to people of all castes.
He advised renouncing desires and surrendering to God.
